settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: extractFile delegates path resolution to FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) rather than raw string concatenation, so path handling is not done manually here.

AbstractZipUnArchiver introduces a ZipEntryFileInfo.getName() that prefers the UnicodePathExtraField unicode name (lines 86-102), but isSelected() is still applied before extraction (line 174, and in the path-based execute at line 241).
isOverwrite()/lastModified check (line 313) only affects overwrite behavior, not location.
candidates.description: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile() builds the on-disk destination as `File f = FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName)` (line 309) and then, without any explicit check that the resolved path stays inside the destination directory, calls dirF.mkdirs() (line 322), f.mkdirs() for directories (line 331), and `new FileOutputStream(f)` plus IOUtil.copy for regular files (lines 338-340). entryName is the archive entry name (from ZipArchiveEntry/ZipEntryFileInfo.getName in AbstractZipUnArchiver, lines 93-95 / 178-181), which is attacker-controlled when an untrusted archive is extracted. If the plexus-utils 3.1.0 FileUtils.resolveFile does not fully neutralize `..` segments or absolute entry names, a crafted entry name can direct writes outside destDirectory (classic archive path-traversal / 'zip slip' pattern). This file contains no defense-in-depth check such as comparing canonical paths or rejecting names containing '..'; the only validation in validate() (lines 181-220) concerns source/destination definition, not entry containment.
missing_evidence: The implementation body of org.codehaus.plexus.util.FileUtils.resolveFile is not present in this repository (plexus-utils 3.1.0 is an external dependency per pom.xml lines 57-61); its exact normalization/handling of '..', leading '/', Windows-style separators, and drive letters could not be inspected, so actual traversal capability is unconfirmed.
No test in the readable set exercises a crafted '../' entry name; no adversarial fixture was read.
Whether callers (e.g. Maven plugin/config surface) pass attacker-controlled archives into this extract() path was not verified.
preconditions: A caller extracts an archive whose entry names are not fully trusted (untrusted zip/tar/jar input).
The external plexus-utils FileUtils.resolveFile version in use does not prevent escaping the base directory for '..' or absolute entry names.
The destDirectory (or destFile) directory is used as the extraction root with the process having write permission outside it (or in a shared directory).
candidates.title: Archive entry extraction path is resolved only via FileUtils.resolveFile with no canonical/long-form containment check in extractFile

counter_evidence: symlink creation is gated by !StringUtils.isEmpty(symlinkDestination) and the symlink only occurs for entries whose ZipEntryFileInfo.isSymbolicLink() is true (resolveSymlink returns null otherwise, lines 211-214).

The destination link path itself is still produced via FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) (line 309), so the link's own location is the same resolution as normal entries (subject to same unresolved external behavior).
candidates.description: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile() receives symlinkDestination and, when it is non-empty, calls `SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(f, new File(symlinkDestination))` (line 327) with the target used verbatim. In AbstractZipUnArchiver this value comes from resolveSymlink()/zf.getUnixSymlink(ze) (lines 204-215) and is passed straight through extractFileIfIncluded (lines 217-222) for both execute() variants (lines 178-181 and 250-253). Because the target is not validated (no check that it is relative to the destination, contains no '..', and is not absolute), a malicious archive can create a link whose target points outside the extraction directory; a subsequent regular entry that resolves under that link name would then be written through the link, potentially overwriting an arbitrary file the extracting user can write. Nothing in the readable source rejects absolute or parent-relative link targets.
missing_evidence: SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink is in plexus components (external, org.codehaus.plexus.components.io.attributes.SymlinkUtils import line 29); its behavior (whether it validates the target, uses relative links, or refuses absolute targets) was not readable in this repository.
No source span in the allowed set shows a post-creation verification that the link target lies inside destDirectory.
Whether typical callers extract untrusted archives with the privileges needed to make traversal consequential was not established.
preconditions: An untrusted archive containing a unix-symlink entry (with attacker-chosen link target) is extracted.
Extraction runs without ignorePermissions and on a filesystem/platform where SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink creates real symlinks.
A later entry in the same archive (or a later extraction) writes to a path that resolves through the created link to a location outside destDirectory.
candidates.title: Symlink targets taken verbatim from the archive are created without any containment or absolute-target check

counter_evidence: isSelected(ze.getName(), fileInfo) is checked first (line 241) and can restrict which entries are processed when file selectors are configured.
The path-based execute is a separate entry point; the no-argument execute() (lines 160-186) extracts all selected entries regardless of any prefix.
candidates.description: AbstractZipUnArchiver.execute(String path, File outputDirectory) includes a zip entry only if `ze.getName().startsWith(path)` (line 246) and then extracts it under outputDirectory (lines 248-256) with no path normalization or containment check on either the filter prefix or the entry name. Two related concerns follow from this source: (a) the filter is a raw string prefix test rather than a path-boundary test, so a prefix such as 'foo' would also match 'foobar/evil'; and (b) even after filtering, the extracted destination is derived from the raw entry name via extractFileIfIncluded -> extractFile with the same unvalidated FileUtils.resolveFile resolution. The actual write location therefore again depends on the external resolveFile behavior plus this non-boundary-aware selection.
missing_evidence: The semantics of the caller-supplied `path` (e.g. whether it always includes a trailing separator) are not visible in the readable spans, so whether the prefix-vs-boundary weakness is reachable in practice is unconfirmed.
FileUtils.resolveFile behavior (external dependency) again determines whether extracted paths can escape the output directory.
No caller code in the allowed spans was read to confirm what values flow into `path`.
preconditions: A caller uses the (path, outputDirectory) extraction entry point with a path prefix.
An untrusted archive contains entries crafted to match the prefix while escaping the intended subtree (and resolveFile does not neutralize traversal).
The output directory is writable and the process has write access outside the intended subtree.
candidates.title: Path-filtered extraction selects entries by raw startsWith on entry names with no normalization

counter_evidence: The directories are constrained by being resolved relative to dotFileDirectory via new File(dotFileDirectory, s[0]) and addDirectory is a normal archiver API; no direct file-system escape primitive is used in this class.
This is an archiving/inclusion path, not a file-write path, so it does not by itself write outside any destination.
candidates.description: DotDirectiveArchiveFinalizer.finalizeArchiveCreation() lists files matching the dot-file prefix in a directory (line 49), reads each line, splits on ':' (line 59), and for both the one-field and two-field forms constructs `new File(dotFileDirectory, s[0])` and calls archiver.addDirectory(directory) or archiver.addDirectory(directory, s[1]) (lines 61-83) without validating the parsed values. The second token s[1] is used as an archive-entry prefix and only receives a trailing slash appended if missing (lines 75-82). If an attacker can place/modify a .plxarc file in the scanned directory (the class comment explicitly states dot files are used to 'communicate archive creation instructions between processes using dot files'), directive lines can select arbitrary directories relative to dotFileDirectory for inclusion into the archive and can control entry prefix strings, i.e. a directive-injection / unintended-content-disclosure concern during archive creation rather than extraction.
missing_evidence: Whether any real caller wires an attacker-influenceable directory into DotDirectiveArchiveFinalizer's constructor was not verified in the readable spans.
The behavior of archiver.addDirectory regarding path validation of the second argument (entry prefix) is outside the read set.
No code in the allowed spans shows how dotFileDirectory is chosen at runtime.
preconditions: The scanned directory (dotFileDirectory) or its .plxarc files are writable by, or influenceable by, an untrusted party.
A DotDirectiveArchiveFinalizer configured with that directory is active during archive creation.
The directories referenced by the directive (resolved relative to dotFileDirectory) contain files whose inclusion is sensitive.
candidates.title: Dot-directive finalizer trusts parsed .plxarc content and passes directory strings to archiver without validation
